note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 by an independent judge (authored none of the tests). Section 3: "An implementation SHOULD provide a configuration knob to specify the maximum number of paths to accept from a sender." Both halves are now proven. Knob: TestParsePeerCapabilityPathsLimit and TestConfiguredPathsLimitOpen (unchanged) show limit { receive N; } at container and per-family level decides the advertised tuples, an omitted limit advertising none. Accept ceiling: the knob reaches session_negotiate.go initPathsLimitRecv(Encoding.PathsLimitRecv), and session_read.go calls receiveCeiling before checkPrefixLimits and delivery, which filters NLRIs admitPath refuses at len(prefix.ids) >= f.limit. test/plugin/paths-limit-receive-ceiling.ci drives it end to end from config: with receive 2, the plugin sees ids 1 and 2 of 10.0.0.0/8 plus 20.0.0.0/8 in one exact event line (positive, also proving the other prefix is untouched), id 3 only after a withdrawal of admitted id 1 frees a slot, and never id 4 (negative; reject=path-id 4). TestProcessMessageRefusesPathOverReceiveCeiling asserts the exact delivered path list through processMessage and the admitted/refused counts 2/1; TestReceiveCeilingAdmitsUpToLimit asserts exact admitted ids [1 2 7], refused counter 1, and a replacement at the ceiling kept. Positive inputs are conforming (at or under the ceiling), negatives exceed this ceiling and no neighbouring rule; assertions are exact, not floors. Discrimination records for all six tags observed red under admitPath breaks: ceiling check -> false (negatives) and limit -> limit-1 (positives).
